sentences.text:
Present:
 Mr. Vikas Bahuguna, Advocate for the appellants.
 Mr. Vijay Khanduri, Brief Holder for the State.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J.(Oral)

The appellant Akashdeep has challenged his conviction and sentence under Section 304B, 498A IPC and Section 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 recorded on 18.11.2023, in Sessions Trial No. 08 of 2016, State of Uttarakhand Vs. Akashdeep and another, by the court of 6th Additional Sessions Judge, Dehradun.

entities.text: State of Uttarakhand Vs. Akashdeep and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He seeks his bail.

2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
Heard on Bail Application No. 1 of 2025 3.
According to the prosecution case, the appellant and the deceased were married on 18.11.2023.
But after marriage, the deceased was harassed and tortured for and in connection with demand of dowry.
Finally, the victim died on 31.07.2024.

4. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant was on bail during trial; he has never misused the bail; according to the statements of the witnesses, there was no demand of dowry till the marriage; even the informant is not categorical as to what kind of demand was made; he has been examined as PW1; sister of the informant who has been examined as PW2 stated that no demand was made in her presence; there is no specific averments with regard to any demand that has been made by the appellant.

1

entities.text: Akashdeep And Another ... vs State Of Uttarakhand on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. Learned State counsel would submit that PW3 Rohit Arya has stated that the demand of dowry was made from the deceased, who had telephonically informed him.
He admits that there has been no specific role, as such; assigned to the appellant.
6. Having considered, without adverting much on merits, this Court is of the view that it is a case in which the execution of sentence should be suspended and the appellant be enlarged on bail.
7. The bail application is allowed.
8. The sentence appealed against is suspended during the pendency of the appeal.

9. The appellant Akashdeep be released on bail, during the pendency of the appeal, on his executing a personal bond and furnishing two reliable sureties, each of the like amount, to the satisfaction of the court concerned.
10. List in due course.

(Ravindra Maithani, J.) 08.07.2025 Jitendra Akashdeep And Another ... vs State Of Uttarakhand on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52672033/
